# niṣkāma karma: action without craving for its fruit — Meaning & Sources | Philosophy Defined

> action without craving for its fruit. The Gītā's practical doctrine: act, and act fully, but do not let the action be motivated by its result.

Glossary

## niṣkāma karma निष्काम कर्म

action without craving for its fruit

Sanskrit · glossed in English

[Glossary](https://www.philosophydef.com/glossary) / niṣkāma karma

A term is not a word. It is a working part of somebody's argument, and the English word usually offered for it is a compromise. This page gives the compromise, the argument, and the reading the sources do not support.

Where it is filed: [Action](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/action) · [Desire](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/desire) · [Freedom](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/freedom) · [Practice](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/practice) · [Equanimity](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/equanimity) · [Responsibility](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/responsibility)

### What the term does

The Gītā's practical doctrine: act, and act fully, but do not let the action be motivated by its result. The point is not that results do not matter but that the agent's relation to them is what determines whether the action binds. Since the results are not within one's control, tying one's satisfaction to them guarantees disturbance whether or not they arrive. This is why the Gītā can present the same act as liberating for one person and binding for another, and why it is a teaching about agency rather than about the content of the act.

### The reading the sources do not support

Read as indifference to outcomes, and so as an alibi for carelessness. The Gītā requires the act to be performed properly and completely; what is given up is the claim on the result, not the effort in the doing.
